heroHeadline: France Opens Criminal Probe into Flotilla Activists' Treatment; IDF Kills Hamas Brigade Commanders in Gaza City; Channel 12 Poll Shows Netanyahu Coalition at 51 Seats
heroSubtitle: France's Foreign Ministry asked the public prosecutor's office on May 29, 2026 to open a criminal investigation into the treatment of French nationals detained after the Gaza flotilla interception — joining Italy's kidnapping and sexual assault probe. The IDF confirmed killing Hamas Gaza City Brigade Deputy Commander Imad Aslim alongside Northern Gaza Brigade leader Izz al-Din Bik in a single strike on May 28, continuing its campaign of eliminating Hamas commanders following the deaths of two successive Qassam Brigades chiefs (May 15 and May 26). The UN added Israel to its conflict-related sexual violence blacklist on May 28, drawing immediate Israeli condemnation. A Channel 12 election poll published by Haaretz on May 29 projects Netanyahu's coalition at just 51 seats (10 short of a majority), with Eisenkot's Yashar party at 17 — underscoring the coalition's fragility ahead of expected October 2026 elections. The post-ceasefire Palestinian death toll in Gaza continues to climb, with Israel controlling ~60% of Gaza beyond the ceasefire Yellow Line.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, Middle East Eye, CNN, The National, Euronews, CBC News, NBC News, FDD, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
